subject: pharmacology
title: Pituitary Pharmacology: Growth Hormone, Somatostatin Analogues, Prolactin and GnRH Agents, Oxytocin and Vasopressin

steps.tx: **Growth hormone** (somatropin, recombinant human GH) replaces deficiency in children (height velocity) and adults (body composition, bone and quality of life), and serves Turner syndrome, chronic kidney disease growth failure and other licensed niches, dosed daily subcutaneously against IGF 1 levels. **Mecasermin**, recombinant IGF 1, rescues severe primary IGF 1 deficiency where GH cannot work, with hypoglycaemia as its shadow. GH excess, not deficiency, occupies the therapeutic second half of this lesson.
steps.say: Somatropin replaces what the pituitary withholds; dose it against IGF 1 and growth, not enthusiasm.

vis.alt: Acromegaly growth hormone and IGF 1 axis diagram
vis.caption: The GH IGF 1 axis that somatropin replaces and acromegaly therapy suppresses at three different levels.

steps.tx: **Octreotide** and lanreotide, somatostatin analogues preferring SSTR2 receptors, suppress growth hormone (and TSH, insulin, glucagon and gut peptides) for acromegaly control, neuroendocrine tumour symptom and hormone syndromes, variceal bleeding (splanchnic vasoconstriction) and pancreatic fistula niches. Monthly depot injections anchor adherence. Gallstones from gallbladder stasis, steatorrhoea, glucose excursions in both directions and bradycardia write their review list.
steps.say: Octreotide is somatostatin with staying power: acromegaly, hormone syndromes and varices share its brake pedal.

left.title: Somatostatin analogue territory
points: Acromegaly: GH and IGF 1 suppression
Neuroendocrine tumours: symptom and growth control
Acute variceal bleeding adjunct
Monthly long acting depot formulations

right.title: Analogue adverse set
points: Gallstones and biliary sludge
Steatorrhoea and fat soluble vitamin loss
Hyper or hypoglycaemia by tumour context
Bradycardia and injection site reactions

steps.tx: **Pegvisomant**, a growth hormone receptor antagonist (pegylated modified GH that occupies without activating), normalises IGF 1 in acromegaly resistant to or intolerant of somatostatin analogues, while GH levels rise uselessly behind the blockade, so IGF 1 alone steers dosing. Tumour size is watched by imaging because the pituitary adenoma loses GH feedback. Liver enzyme monitoring and daily injection burden complete its specialist profile.
steps.say: Pegvisomant blocks the receptor and lets GH shout unheard; steer it by IGF 1 and image the tumour.

nodes.label: IGF 1 normalises, GH rises behind blockade
Adenoma imaged periodically, liver enzymes monitored

steps.tx: Dopamine agonists treat the pituitary from the hypothalamic side: **cabergoline** (long acting, twice weekly) and bromocriptine suppress prolactin secretion from lactotroph adenomas, shrinking most prolactinomas and restoring gonadal function, first line ahead of surgery for most. **Hyperprolactinaemia** differentials (pregnancy, hypothyroidism, dopamine blocking drugs, stalk compression with its modest elevations) must be sorted before lifelong labels attach, and macroprolactin assays unmask laboratory artefacts.
steps.say: Cabergoline shrinks prolactinomas better than surgery for most; exclude pregnancy, thyroid and drug causes first.

vis.alt: Cabergoline dopamine agonist illustration for hyperprolactinaemia
vis.caption: Cabergoline, the long acting dopamine agonist that is first line therapy for prolactinoma. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **GnRH analogues** exploit pulse physiology: continuous leuprolide or goserelin first flare gonadotropins (a week of worsening prostate cancer or precocious puberty symptoms) then downregulate receptors into medical castration, serving prostate cancer, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, precocious puberty and IVF protocols, with add back oestrogen strategies protecting bone in long gynaecological use. Antagonists **degarelix** and relugolix skip the flare entirely where spinal cord compression or symptoms forbid it.
steps.say: Continuous GnRH first flares then castrates; antagonists skip the flare where cancer cannot afford it.

left.title: GnRH agonists (leuprolide, goserelin)
points: Initial flare over about a week
Then receptor downregulation and suppression
Depot monthly to quarterly formulations
Add back therapy protects bone in long use

right.title: GnRH antagonists (degarelix, relugolix)
points: Immediate suppression, no flare
Prostate cancer where flare is dangerous
Oral relugolix daily or degarelix injections
Histamine type injection reactions with degarelix

steps.tx: **Acromegaly** therapy assembles the lesson's three levels in guideline order: transsphenoidal surgery first where resectable, somatostatin analogues as primary medical therapy and tumour control, pegvisomant for IGF 1 normalisation in resistance (often combined), cabergoline for mild disease especially with prolactin co secretion, and radiotherapy as the slow last line. Biochemical targets (IGF 1 normalisation, GH thresholds) and comorbidity clinics (cardiac, metabolic, sleep apnoea, colon) define success beyond the hormone printout.
steps.say: Surgery, somatostatin, pegvisomant, cabergoline for the mild: acromegaly is a ladder, not a drug.

nodes.label: Pegvisomant added or substituted for IGF 1 control
Cabergoline for mild or prolactin co secreting disease

steps.tx: Posterior pituitary pharmacology pairs **oxytocin** (labour induction and augmentation, postpartum haemorrhage prevention and treatment, with hypotension and water intoxication at infusion excess from its ADH like structure) against **vasopressin** and desmopressin from the diuretic lessons (V1 pressor rescue, V2 water conservation). Terlipressin, a vasopressin prodrug, serves variceal bleeding and hepatorenal syndrome where splanchnic constriction is the therapeutic point.
steps.say: Oxytocin contracts uterus and, in careless infusion volumes, retains water; vasopressin's family runs pressure and urine on separate receptors.

left.title: Oxytocin territory
points: Labour induction and augmentation protocols
Postpartum haemorrhage prevention and treatment
Hypotension with rapid bolus, tachycardia
Water intoxication with prolonged high volume infusions

right.title: Vasopressin family recap
points: Vasopressin: V1 pressor in shock, varices via terlipressin
Desmopressin: V2, central diabetes insipidus, von Willebrand release
Tolvaptan: V2 blockade from the diuretic lessons
Receptor geography predicts every indication

steps.tx: Bromocriptine's second career in acromegaly and its first in prolactinoma share dopamine's pituitary logic, while **cabergoline** at Parkinson doses (previous module) imported valvular fibrosis surveillance from the ergot family, a dose dependent concern largely spared at endocrine micro doses. Quinagolide offers a non ergot dopamine agonist alternative where ergot effects forbid. Every pituitary prescription in this lesson is therefore also a cardiac, hepatic or pregnancy conversation scheduled in advance.
steps.say: Endocrine cabergoline doses spare valves that Parkinson doses threaten; dose writes the surveillance.

left.title: Dopamine agonists in pituitary disease
points: Cabergoline twice weekly: prolactinoma first line
Bromocriptine: older, shorter acting, more nausea
Quinagolide: non ergot alternative
Restore gonadal function and shrink tumour

right.title: Surveillance by dose
points: Endocrine doses: fibrosis risk low, periodic review
Parkinson doses: echocardiographic valve surveillance
Impulse control effects shared with agonist class
Pregnancy: tumour expansion vigilance, drug often stopped
